issues.body:
The diff rewrites ROLE_BY_KIND from {"security": "soundness"} to {"security": "impl"}. The stated rationale is that trust surfaces are carried by orchestration/routing.toml's higher-precedence match_labels route rather than by a synthetic role — which I verified is true for AREA labels (dispatch/worker/set-up-account/review-loop/groom/zk/mpc/crypto/auth/e2ee). It is NOT true for the `kind:security` label itself: "kind:security" contains none of those keywords, so an issue labelled e.g. `kind:security` + `area:usage` matches no security route.

Resolution for that issue after this change (verified against scripts/route-resolve.py resolve() and scripts/policy-resolve.py resolve()): Phase 1 security match fails, Phase 2 picks role_routes["impl"] -> model_chain [sol, opus5, fable, opus], agent registry-impl, escalate=false. Before the change it derived role "soundness" -> [opus5, opus], agent registry-reviewer, escalate=true (chain exhaustion escalates to a human instead of degrading).

So the one label whose entire purpose is to say "this is a security issue" now routes to the ordinary implementation lane with no escalation and no soundness tier. No self-test in the diff exercises ROLE_BY_KIND["security"] in either the old or the new form, so the change is both unjustified in the PR text and uncovered by tests.
issues.fix_hint:
Pick one and test it:
(a) Add "security" to the match_labels keyword list in orchestration/routing.toml's security-override route. This is the semantically correct option — it puts kind:security back on [opus5, opus] + escalate=true AND (deliberately) makes the arm-side classifier treat such PRs as trust-surface. Note the standing caution in the file about not polluting match_labels: it applies to UI/infra keywords that would human-arm unrelated PRs; "security" is not that case.
(b) Keep ROLE_BY_KIND["security"] pointing at a role whose route in routing.toml sets escalate = true.
Either way add a self-test asserting the routing outcome, e.g. resolve(triage-derived labels for ["kind:security", "area:usage", "priority:P1"]) yields escalate=True and the opus5-led chain — not merely that _role() returns some string.
issues.title: ROLE_BY_KIND["security"] -> "impl" silently drops kind:security issues out of any escalating/soundness lane

issues.body:
This PR moves the trust-surface posture from a triage-side role to a routing-side match_labels rule, and deletes the `role = "soundness"` route. The correctness of that move rests entirely on an invariant that is asserted nowhere: every role _role() can emit must exist as a role route in orchestration/routing.toml.

That invariant is load-bearing and fails hard, not softly. scripts/route-resolve.py raises UnknownRoleError ("a single role with NO explicit role route") and scripts/policy-resolve.py raises PolicyError(f"unknown role {role!r}") for any role absent from role_routes. scripts/dispatch-plan.py catches it per-issue and drops the issue with a stderr line, so a mismatch produces a permanently invisible, silently skipped issue every tick — precisely the stranding class this PR sets out to repair.

The new end-to-end test only reaches ready-issues.compute_ready(), which accepts ANY `role:.+` (ready-issues.py has_role uses the regex ^role:.+$). It therefore passes identically under the old soundness behaviour and cannot detect a triage/routing divergence. That makes it a weak test of the changed behaviour, not a guard on it.
issues.fix_hint: Extend _self_test() to load orchestration/routing.toml and assert every emittable role resolves, e.g. for each role in set(ROLE_BY_KIND.values()) | set(ROLE_BY_TYPE.values()) | {"site", "ci"}: route_resolve.resolve([f"role:{role}", "area:usage"], doc) does not raise. Add one case asserting the trust-surface outcome directly: resolve(["role:impl", "area:worker"], doc) == (["opus5", "opus"], "registry-reviewer", True), which is the property this PR claims replaces the soundness role. Non-vacuous: both assertions go red the moment triage and routing drift apart again.
issues.title: No self-test asserts that the role triage emits is resolvable by orchestration/routing.toml — the exact invariant this PR now depends on

issues.body:
The new guard is enforced solely in main() after argparse. scripts/retriage.py does `import triage as static_triage` and calls `classify(labels, "task", trusted=True)` (triage() directly) at line 32, returning result["add"] verbatim from plan(). .github/workflows/retriage.yml then applies those labels every 30 minutes:

    while IFS= read -r label; do args+=(--add-label "$label"); done < <(jq -r '.add[]' <<<"$decision")
    gh issue edit "$number" -R "$REPO" "${args[@]}"

No --defined-labels, no vocabulary check. So the label-vocabulary drift that this PR declares must "fail closed" is unguarded on the scheduled promotion path — the higher-volume of the two paths. (retriage.yml at least batches add+remove into one gh call under set -e, so it aborts rather than half-applying; but the guard's diagnostic — "triage would add undefined repository label(s): X" — is exactly what makes such a failure debuggable, and it is absent there.)
issues.fix_hint: Enforce inside the library rather than at the CLI edge: give triage() an optional defined_labels parameter that calls validate_add_labels() when supplied, and have retriage.plan() accept/propagate it (retriage.yml can fetch `gh label list ... --json name` once per sweep and pass it in). Then add a self-test asserting retriage.plan() raises/skips on an undefined add-label, so the guard cannot be reintroduced as CLI-only.
issues.title: validate_add_labels() is opt-in at the CLI only — scripts/retriage.py imports triage() and bypasses the drift guard

issues.body:
After this route is removed, `soundness` is absent from role_routes in both resolvers, so any open issue still labelled role:soundness raises UnknownRoleError / PolicyError forever: dispatch-plan.py drops it with a stderr diagnostic every tick and CLAIM would reject it. Neither of the two label-writing paths can repair it — triage._role() returns an explicit single role:* unchanged (so retriage re-emits role:soundness), and the new repair step's jq filter explicitly excludes any issue that already has a role: label (`select(any($labels[]; startswith("role:")) | not)`).

Honest caveat: the in-repo evidence suggests few or no such issues exist. The old workflow added labels one at a time with `|| true`, so if `role:soundness` was never created in the repo's label vocabulary its adds failed silently — which is the most likely origin of the roleless status:ready issues this PR repairs, and implies the label was never actually applied. I cannot verify live label state from the checkout, and the diff neither documents this reasoning nor guards against the case.
issues.fix_hint: Cheapest belt-and-braces: in _role(), translate a legacy explicit role — `if explicit[0] == "soundness": return "impl"` — with a self-test asserting triage(["role:soundness", "priority:P1", "area:worker"]) emits role:impl and puts role:soundness in remove. Alternatively drop the `startswith("role:")` exclusion in the repair jq for the specific value role:soundness. Either way, state in the PR body whether `role:soundness` exists in the live label vocabulary.
issues.title: Deleting the soundness role route leaves no migration path for an issue that already carries role:soundness

issues.body: The diff correctly turns a failed add into `exit 1`, but leaves the remove loop as `|| true` in the same step (line 83), while the new repair step's remove loop (line 105) fails loudly under set -e. The asymmetry matters: the removes are not cosmetic. When triage promotes an issue it emits REMOVE: status:untriaged, and ready-issues.py lists status:untriaged in BUSY_STATUS — so an issue that ends up with status:ready AND status:untriaged is filtered out of ready_candidates() and never dispatched. A silently swallowed remove therefore produces exactly the invisible-stranded-issue failure this PR exists to fix, just via the other label.
issues.fix_hint: Make the two steps consistent: apply the same `|| { echo "::error::failed to remove label ..."; exit 1; }` treatment to the remove loop in the Static triage step. Better still, batch the plan into a single `gh issue edit` with repeated --add-label/--remove-label args (as .github/workflows/retriage.yml already does), so the mutation is all-or-nothing rather than per-label partial.
issues.title: Static triage hard-fails on a failed --add-label but still swallows --remove-label failures, which strands the issue

issues.body: The group is `triage-${{ github.event.issue.number }}`. On a workflow_dispatch run there is no github.event.issue, so the group is the constant `triage-` and cancel-in-progress is true. A second manual dispatch therefore cancels an in-flight repair run mid-loop, after it has already edited some issues, leaving the rest unrepaired with no record beyond a cancelled job. The repair loop is not idempotent-unsafe (a re-run redoes the work), so this is recoverable, but the cancellation is silent and the step summary is never written.
issues.fix_hint: Give the dispatch path its own non-cancelling group, e.g. group: triage-${{ github.event.issue.number || 'repair' }} plus cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'issues' }} — matching the pattern .github/workflows/retriage.yml already uses (cancel-in-progress: false for a sweep job).
issues.title: concurrency group collapses to "triage-" on workflow_dispatch with cancel-in-progress: true

issues.body: `repaired=$((repaired + 1))` runs once per iteration regardless of whether the triage plan was empty, so the summary line "Roleless ready issues found: N; repaired: N" is always a tautology and conveys no information about what actually changed. It also cannot distinguish "promoted to a role" from "demoted to status:untriaged" — a demotion is a materially different outcome an operator would want to see.
issues.fix_hint: Increment only when the plan is non-empty (`[ -n "$add$rem" ] && repaired=$((repaired + 1))`), and echo the per-issue plan into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (e.g. "#$num add=[$add] remove=[$rem]") so the manual run leaves an auditable trail of which issues it touched.
issues.title: `repaired` is incremented unconditionally, so the step summary always reports repaired == found

issues.body: --defined-labels (and the pre-existing --labels) are split on "," while the workflow builds them with jq join(","). GitHub label names may legitimately contain both commas and spaces. A comma-bearing label is split into fragments, so validate_add_labels() could reject a plan whose labels are in fact defined; a space-bearing label would additionally be re-split by the workflow's `for l in $add`. The failure direction is closed (the step errors rather than mislabelling), so this is low severity — but the guard's diagnostic would be actively misleading.
issues.fix_hint: Use a separator that cannot appear in a label (newline or NUL) end to end: jq -r '.[].name' piped through a `--defined-labels-file`/stdin, and iterate adds with `while IFS= read -r l` instead of `for l in $add`. If the comma format is kept, note the constraint in the --defined-labels help text.
issues.title: Comma-split label parsing and unquoted shell word-splitting break on labels containing commas or spaces

verdict.summary:
The core premise of the change checks out: I verified that BOTH resolvers evaluate security routes before role routes (scripts/route-resolve.py resolve() Phase 1, scripts/policy-resolve.py resolve() iterates security_routes before role_routes/defaults), so deleting the synthetic `soundness` role does NOT weaken model selection or the arm gate for issues carrying a trust-surface area label — orchestration/routing.toml's match_labels keyword set is untouched, and the arm-side classifier reads that same set. The repair step, the required --defined-labels vocabulary guard, and the hard-fail on a failed --add-label are all genuine fail-closed improvements, and the new self-tests are non-vacuous (the vocabulary guard has both an accept and a reject case; the ready-issues end-to-end case flips red if the plan stops promoting).

But the change is not complete, and one part of it is a security-relevant downgrade:

1. ROLE_BY_KIND["security"] now maps to "impl". A `kind:security` issue that carries no dispatch/worker/set-up-account/review-loop/groom/zk/mpc/crypto/auth/e2ee label matches NO match_labels route, so it now resolves to the plain impl route (sol-led chain, agent registry-impl, escalate=false) instead of the escalating soundness chain. Nothing in the diff compensates, and no self-test covers ROLE_BY_KIND["security"] at all.

2. The self-tests never assert the invariant this PR actually relies on — that the role triage emits is a role routing.toml can resolve. Both resolvers raise on an unknown role, so a triage/routing mismatch is a silent per-tick strand (dispatch-plan.py skips the issue to stderr); a one-line cross-check would have made the soundness removal self-verifying.

3. validate_add_labels() is enforced only on triage.py's CLI path. scripts/retriage.py imports triage() directly and .github/workflows/retriage.yml applies result["add"] every 30 minutes with no vocabulary check, so the drift guard does not cover the main promotion path.… [truncated 169 chars]
